title: Years of life lost and years lived with disability

draft.title: Years of life lost and years lived with disability
card: One DALY is one year of healthy life lost. DALYs are made of two parts added together: DALY = YLL + YLD.
years of life lost to early death. It counts the years a person would have been expected to live if they had not died early.
years lived with disability. It counts the years spent living with an illness or injury, adjusted for how much the condition reduces health.
A condition that rarely kills but lasts for years mostly adds YLD. A condition that kills people young mostly adds YLL.
draft.remember: DALY = YLL + YLD: years lost to early death plus years lived in poor health.

a.q: Which part of the DALY measure counts the years a person spends living with asthma?
a.why: YLD counts years lived with illness or disability, and asthma is an ongoing condition. YLL is tempting, but it counts only years lost because of early death.
a.clue: The person is alive during these years.

b.q: In a region of Victoria, a type of arthritis causes pain and limited movement for many people for decades, but few die from it. How will its burden mostly be counted?
opts: Mostly as YLD, because people live long with it
Mostly as YLL, because it affects many people
Mostly as YLL, because it lasts for many years
Mostly as YLD, because it causes many early deaths
b.why: Few people die from the condition, so few years are lost to early death and YLL stays low. The years spent living with pain and limited movement add YLD, so most of its DALYs come from YLD.
b.clue: Ask whether the burden comes from dying early or from living with the condition.

b.best: Mostly as YLD, because people live long with it
